evals.prompt: A Docs issue asks: 'People keep asking how to add a second code repository to an existing fab0 project. Document it.' Which Diátaxis kind is this page, which folder does it go in, and what must it not contain?
evals.expected_output: A how-to page in docs/how-to/. It gives the steps for the goal only (add the repository to repos in fab0.yaml with path, github and owner; check out the sibling; run fab0-resolve validate) and links to explanation/branching.md and reference/project.md instead of explaining design or listing every field.
assertions: Classifies the page as a how-to
Says explanation and full field reference belong on other pages, linked rather than mixed in

evals.prompt: Write the section headings, in order, of the brief for a Docs run whose intent is 'Audit reference/step.md against the core schemas', and give one example finding in the required form.
evals.expected_output: The seven sections in order: Intent, Readers, Sources, Findings, Outline, Acceptance, Open questions. A finding numbered F1 that states what the page says and what the source says, with path:line@sha for both, and whether a docs task fixes it or it needs code.
assertions: Lists exactly Intent, Readers, Sources, Findings, Outline, Acceptance, Open questions in that order
The example finding has an F-number
The example finding cites both sides as path:line@sha
The example finding says whether it is a docs fix or needs code

evals.prompt: Review this sentence proposed for docs/explanation/gates.md: 'When the reviewer rejects a task, fab0 will simply re-run the implementer as many times as needed until it is approved, and a person then always merges the PR.' The pipeline schema says an auto gate's `retry` defaults to 2 and `then` to `human`, and that with `merge: auto` the engine's `apply` merges the unit within `git.auto_merge`.
evals.expected_output: A reject with findings: the claim is false on two counts (re-runs stop at the gate's retry, 2 by default, then `then` decides, a person by default; with `merge: auto`, apply merges the approved unit, within the merge policy, so a person doesn't always merge), plus style findings (future tense 'will', filler 'simply', 'PR' instead of 'pull request').
assertions: Flags the unlimited re-run claim as false, citing the retry limit and what follows it
Flags 'a person always merges' as false: with merge: auto, apply merges within the policy
Notes at least one style or vocabulary issue (future tense, 'simply', or 'PR')
The verdict is reject, not approve

evals.prompt: A page says: '`call` runs another pipeline as a child run.' `fab0-resolve validate` refuses `call` until a factory needs it. How should the page say it?
evals.expected_output: Mark it Planned, for example '**Planned:** `call` runs another pipeline as a child run', and say what exists today: validate checks its shape and refuses it.
assertions: States that validate refuses it today
